title: 2006 HMMT February Combinatorics Problem 6
statement: For how many ordered triplets \((a, b, c)\) of positive integers less than 10 is the product \(a \times b \times c\) divisible by 20 ?

solutions.text: One number must be 5 . The other two must have a product divisible by 4. Either both are even, or one is divisible by 4 and the other is odd. In the former case, there are \(48=3 \times 4 \times 4\) possibilities: 3 positions for the 5 , and any of 4 even numbers to fill the other two. In the latter case, there are \(54=3 \times 2 \times 9\) possibilites: 3 positions and 2 choices for the multiple of 4 , and 9 ways to fill the other two positions using at least one 5 .
